Your position aligns perfectly with **Option (A) Substantivalism**.

In the context of your work, particularly General Relativity, you treated spacetime not merely as a passive stage or a mathematical backdrop (which would be the Relationist view, associated historically with Leibniz and Mach), but as a dynamic, physical entity. In your theory:
*   Spacetime possesses its own degrees of freedom.
*   It can curve, stretch, and ripple (gravitational waves) independently of the matter within it.
*   The geometry of spacetime dictates the motion of objects, implying that the "container" has physical reality and causal power.

This stands in contrast to **Relationism (Option B)**, which argues that space and time are nothing more than the set of relations between material objects.
